steps.intent: Open the reply composer via the Reply link
Write an AI-generated reply tailored to the email (the recorded text is only an example) into the Message Body
Let the reply auto-save as a draft and wait for the 'Draft saved' notice; never press Send
Return to the inbox via 'Back to Inbox' and repeat for the next unread email

dataFlow.field: sender name / email content (used to personalise reply, e.g. 'Thanks Priya')

successCriteria: Opening a row shows the message view with h2.hP subject and a Reply link
Clicking Reply shows the Message Body textbox
After typing, the 'Draft saved' live notice (#toast) appears
The Drafts count (#dcount) increases by one per email processed
No email is sent: the Send button is never clicked
consequentialActions: Send email (Send button in the reply composer) — STOP-BEFORE: the widget must never press Send; the user only saved a draft

strategyHints.reason: Rows are DOM elements with stable data-legacy-message-id; no network calls observed
Email content is read from the rendered message view
Reply link has a unique aria-label; no network observed
Text must be entered into a contenteditable textbox; no network observed
Draft save is confirmed only by the live 'Draft saved' toast and #dcount; no network observed
Back to Inbox is a DOM button; no network observed

openQuestions: Should the widget draft replies for all unread emails or only the currently open / newest N?
What tone or length should the AI-written replies use?
Should emails that already have a draft reply be skipped?
